apparatus.basis: Editor's restoration of one letter; standard qualitative ⲛⲉⲥⲉ- ('be beautiful') agreeing with ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'his beauty.'
Text physically present but lexeme uncertain; tentatively rendered 'rulers/principalities' from context paralleling ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' as worldly cosmic authorities. See note.
Editor's restoration of final ⲍ; from ⲙⲟⲩⲍ = ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill, fullness.' Confirmed by following clause 'when it is full in him' (ⲉⲧϥⲙⲏⲍ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϥ).
Editor's restoration; standard expression ⲍⲏ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'in the cosmos' parallels lines 2, 14, 17, 31.
Editor's restoration; the explanatory clause 'because his light is exalted...' parallels lines 13-14.
Editor's restoration; ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ ('the aeons,' Lyc. plural with epenthetic ϩ) is the expected referent for the heavenly light surpassed only by the Father's.

notes.decision: The ordinals are written with doubled article ⲧⲧ-, marking the feminine ordinal series throughout. Translated as 'The first / The second / The third...' enumerating five attributes of the Father followed by three further 'types' revealed in the sun. The doubled-article form is a Lycopolitan dialectal feature already attested in this corpus.
Translated as 'his light, because he gives-light through his light': ϥ̄ⲧⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ is causative ⲧⲣⲉ-ⲣ̄-ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'cause to give light' = 'illuminate'; ⲍⲏ̄ taken as instrumental 'through.'

Parsed ϣⲁϩ as the Lycopolitan habitual prefix (= Sah. ϣⲁϥ-) on verb ϣⲱⲗ. The verb ϣⲱⲗ is rendered 'pour forth / spread out / shed' from context (the sun habitually distributing beauty and uprightness over creation). Crum lists ϣⲱⲗ as a verb of distributive action; semantic precision low.
Lycopolitan ⲍ for ⲥ: ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟⲩⲧⲱⲛ 'uprightness, rectitude, straightness.' The pairing with 'beauty' suggests aesthetic-moral order — the regular, upright structure that the sun's light reveals.

The feminine relative ⲧⲉⲧⲉ + habitual ϣⲁϩ-ⲃⲁⲗ-ⲥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ takes 3sg.f object referring back to ⲧϯⲩⲭⲏ 'the soul.' Translated 'whom he habitually releases out from her' — recasting in idiomatic English as 'whom he habitually releases out of all the fruits.' Using 'release' per glossary terminology rule for ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.

The form ϩϯ (and its parallel ⲛ̄ϩ̄ϯ ⲁⲛ) appears to function as a finite verbal form 'he gives' — possibly a Lycopolitan/scribal contraction of ϣⲁϥϯ (habitual) or ⲁϥϯ (perfect). The ϩ may be a graphic variant for ϥ. Translated as present 'he gives.'

The Cross of Light (σταυρὸς τοῦ φωτός) — the Manichaean cosmic figure of dispersed light suffering in matter (the Jesus patibilis), the totality of light-particles bound throughout creation. Receiving 'scent and taste' is consistent with the correspondential register of this kephalaion: each cosmic register IS a sensory mode.

Lexeme of uncertain analysis. Possibly Lyc. ⲛⲁ-ⲟⲩⲣⲡⲉ-ϣⲉ 'those of the (sent ones / dignitaries / officers)' from ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ 'send,' yielding 'envoys/embassies/officials.' Translated 'rulers' in parallel with the immediately preceding ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' — the doublet 'powers and rulers' as cosmic authorities. Confidence low; flagged in apparatus as restoration with proposed reading.

Literally 'she is a great one of days.' Translated 'is great in days' — i.e., great in temporal extent / abundance. The phrase may also evoke the Manichaean cosmological 'Great Days' (ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲟⲩⲉ in glossary), but here functions as the comparative measure of the Father's release-act over against all other dissolutions.

Comparative correspondential clause: 'in the same manner that the disc of the moon does not diminish.' The moon's full disc, even when it appears to wax and wane, retains its true fullness — typological proof of the Father's invariant fullness despite emanating powers and gods.

Reading per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ: 'not to consent / not be like.' Here in the construction 'deficiency does not come to be in him X' — translated 'at all,' taking ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ as an adverbial intensifier of the negation. Could alternatively read 'without measure' (privative ⲁⲧ- + ⲙⲉⲧ-).
